problem: Embodied QA methods typically rely on raw visual input (video/frames) to multimodal models, and it is unclear how well purely textual scene annotations can substitute for visual data when feeding LLMs in 3D environments.
motivation: Text is a compact, LLM-friendly scene representation, but its effectiveness depends on annotation type, detail and context length. The paper systematically studies these factors on OpenEQA to understand what makes textual scene descriptions useful for embodied reasoning.
key_idea: Represent 3D scenes as detailed text annotations (objects, attributes, spatial relations, potential interactions) and feed them to text-only LLMs for EQA, studying context length, annotation structure and model size.
insight: Detailed descriptions with object lists, explicit attributes, spatial relations and possible interactions let text-only LLMs (GPT-4 57.6%, LLaMA-2 58.5%) beat the GPT-4V baseline (55.3%) on the OpenEQA subset. An optimal context length of about 1517 tokens was estimated. Humans still do far worse with text (50%) than with video (86.8%), so text does not fully replace visual perception.
method: Scene annotations: generate text descriptions of scenes of different types (free-form vs structured) including object lists, attributes, spatial relations, potential interactions
LLM evaluation: answer OpenEQA questions from text annotations only, using GPT-4 and LLaMA-2
Context length analysis: estimate optimal annotation length (~1517 tokens)
Model size analysis: compare performance across LLM sizes
Human study: compare human comprehension from text annotations (50%) vs video (86.8%)
